outOfScope: program details of mortgages, auto loans, or student loans

claims.claim: Debt is an amount owed for borrowed funds, typically repaid with interest by a date set in the repayment terms.
Interest on an unpaid balance compounds: interest is charged on the principal plus previously accumulated interest, so the balance grows on its own.
The debt avalanche strategy repays debts in order of interest rate, highest first, while making minimum payments on the others, and it minimizes the total interest paid.
The debt snowball strategy repays debts in order of balance size, smallest first, while making minimum payments on the others.

A debt management plan is arranged through a credit counseling organization: the consumer makes one payment to the organization, which pays the creditors; it typically lowers the monthly payment, may lower interest charges and fees, may lengthen repayment, and cannot erase debts.
Credit counseling organizations are usually non-profits whose trained, certified counselors advise on money and debts and help with budgets.
Paying only the minimum payment keeps the account current but prolongs repayment and increases the total interest paid.
Payment history — whether bills were paid on time — has the greatest impact on credit scores.
Budgeting first, contacting creditors, and stopping adding to debt are the FTC's starting steps for getting out of debt.
Bankruptcy is a last-resort option that can remain on a credit report for about ten years.
Debt settlement differs from credit counseling and carries warning signs, including upfront fees and promises to erase debt.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Which repayment strategy is better: avalanche or snowball
positions: Snowball produces quicker early wins by clearing small balances (Investopedia).
CFPB and FTC publish neither strategy; the names come from financial-education sources.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson names both as common approaches, explicitly says neither is endorsed and the right choice depends on the person, and applies both to the same three debts in the worked example so the trade-off is visible.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Credit counseling versus debt settlement outcomes
positions: Credit counseling organizations arrange DMPs that reduce monthly payments over a longer period (CFPB).
Debt settlement companies negotiate for less than the full amount owed, and the FTC lists warning signs: upfront fees and promises to erase debt.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson describes counseling and DMPs factually, warns that promises to erase debt belong to settlement rather than counseling, and endorses no service.

conflictingEvidence.issue: The exact CFPB wording for the payment-history ranking
positions: The sentence 'Paying your bills on time, every time, has the greatest impact on your score' is widely attributed to CFPB credit-score content.
The live CFPB page is bot-blocked (HTTP 403) and the exact sentence could not be re-located in a specific capture during this pass.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson states the ranking (payment history has the greatest impact) and attributes it to the two verified records that support it — CFPB's factor list naming bill-paying history, and FICO's official statement that payment history is the most important factor — rather than reproducing the unverified quote verbatim.

conflictingEvidence.issue: How long bankruptcy stays on a credit report
positions: Individual credit bureaus may report bankruptcies for a range of years depending on the chapter.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson says 'about ten years' per the FTC without asserting a precise uniform period.

sourceRecords.title: What is credit counseling? (Ask CFPB)
sourceRecords.notes: Tier A. Live page returns HTTP 403 to the fetcher; slug verified against the Internet Archive CDX index (captures 2017-2022) and content read via Wayback capture. Supports: counseling organizations advise on money and debts, help with budgets, and develop debt management plans; organizations are usually non-profit; counselors are certified and trained in consumer credit, money and debt management, and budgeting; a DMP involves one monthly payment to the organization, which pays the creditors; a DMP typically lowers the monthly payment and may reduce interest charges and fees; a DMP cannot erase debts.

sourceRecords.title: What is the difference between credit counseling and debt settlement, debt consolidation, or credit repair? (Ask CFPB)
sourceRecords.notes: Tier A. Read via Wayback capture (live 403; slug verified in the Internet Archive CDX index, captures 2024-2026). Supports: a DMP is a payment plan; the counselor works to lower the overall monthly payment; repayment may be lengthened; interest rates may be lowered; debts cannot be erased; distinguishes counseling from debt settlement, debt consolidation, and credit repair.

sourceRecords.notes: Tier B. Verified live (HTTP 200) on 2026-08-21 and cross-checked against an Internet Archive capture dated 2026-02-03.
